name: Discrete Global Extremum of Vector Cross Products
description: Replaces the local polynomial constraint with a global sum of squared Euclidean norms of cross products. The vectors are chosen such that the squared norm is 17 if the parameters differ, and 0 if they are the same. By requiring the total sum over m hazards to be exactly 17m, the model must deduce that every single hazard must achieve the maximum possible value of 17, which locally enforces s_u != s_v. This defeats pattern matching by requiring a global-to-local deduction step before the bipartite graph structure is revealed.
